answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by anchoring each identity to a living willow planted at a named riverbank plot, its roots weighted by an engraved shale anchor stone. A surveyor verifies the tree and stone once per season, one plot per day, and random spot-checks require the holder to be photographed beside their own willow within a day. Each extra fake identity costs another real plot, another engraved stone, another surveyor day, and a registration fee in outside money that doubles per identity on the same funding trail, so a farm's cost grows faster than its identities.
